gaps.sentence: The report ___ have been finished yesterday; the deadline was missed.
gaps.explanation: 'Should have been finished' — it was expected but did not happen.

gaps.sentence: ___ I borrow your charger for a minute?
gaps.explanation: 'May' is the polite way to ask permission: May I borrow.

gaps.sentence: Visitors ___ to leave the gallery by 6 p.m.
gaps.hint: have to takes the full infinitive
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' takes the full infinitive with 'to': have to leave.

gaps.sentence: You ___ to be more careful with your passwords.
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' behaves like 'should' and always takes 'to': ought to be.

gaps.sentence: The report ___ to be submitted by noon tomorrow.
gaps.explanation: 'Has to' expresses obligation with a third-person subject: has to be.

gaps.sentence: I ___ see the sea from my bedroom window when I was little.
gaps.explanation: Verbs of perception use 'could' for past ability: could see.

gaps.sentence: You have been travelling all day, so you ___ be exhausted.
gaps.hint: an obvious conclusion from known facts
gaps.explanation: A logical conclusion from known facts uses 'must': must be exhausted.

gaps.sentence: If you want a refund, you ___ keep the receipt — no receipt, no refund.
gaps.hint: a necessity that applies in the future
gaps.explanation: Future necessity uses 'will have to': will have to keep.
